tryThisNow: Open a shared spreadsheet and add one decision log row before considering any security: famous name, acquisition growth, financing complexity, and pending evidence.

implementationPlan.title: Keep a Case-History Decision Log
implementationPlan.coreSkill: Use a decision log to slow attractive cases under pressure. Mark whether a famous name hides weak finances or merger problems, whether acquisition growth depends on conglomerate accounting and leverage, and whether layered securities make owner economics hard to see.

ifThenPlans.plan: If a familiar corporate name makes a security feel safe, then add a shared spreadsheet row that checks for weak finances and merger problems before treating prominence as protection.

If rapid acquisition growth is the main reason for approval in an email draft, then pause the send and add a line asking whether conglomerate accounting and leverage make expansion look better than economic reality.
If layered securities make a deal hard to appraise during a calendar block, then leave the decision pending until the log shows who bears the risk and how owner economics can be seen.

implementationPlan.twentyFourHourChallenge: Before the next day ends, create one decision log row for a security that looks attractive. Leave it pending unless the row addresses name prominence, acquisition growth, and financing complexity.
implementationPlan.weeklyPractice: Once a week, repeat the same audit on one active idea. Keep the decision pending when a famous name substitutes for credit analysis, acquisition growth hides leverage, or financing complexity makes owner economics unclear.
